newsItems.title: Sinner and Zverev Set Wimbledon Final After Straight-Sets Semis
newsItems.excerpt: Friday's men's semi-finals at Wimbledon 2026 both went the way of the top two seeds in straight sets. Alexander Zverev ended British wildcard Arthur Fery's fairytale run 7-6 (0), 6-2, 6-4 to reach his first SW19 final and bid for a French Open-Wimbledon double. Defending champion Jannik Sinner then outclassed Novak Djokovic 6-4, 6-4, 6-4, avenging January's Australian Open semi-final defeat with 16 aces and 88% of first-serve points won. Sinner and Zverev meet Sunday in a rematch of the 2025 Australian Open final, while Saturday's women's title match is an all-Czech affair between Karolina Muchova and Linda Noskova.

newsItems.title: Wei Chong and Wooi Yik Debut New Malaysia Doubles Pair at Japan Open
newsItems.excerpt: The DAIHATSU Japan Open Super 750 begins July 14 at Tokyo Metropolitan Gymnasium with a $950,000 purse. Malaysia's reshuffled men's doubles pairing of Man Wei Chong and Olympic bronze medallist Soh Wooi Yik opens against Taiwan's world No. 18 Lee brothers, while Indonesia sends 12 players led by Jonatan Christie and three men's doubles pairs. Reigning champions Goh Sze Fei and Nur Izzuddin start against China's Hu Ke Yuan and Lin Xiang Yi.

newsItems.title: PPA Tour Shifts to Melbourne and Singapore After Tokyo Rankings Shake-Up
newsItems.excerpt: Professional pickleball's global calendar heats up in July with the PPA Australia 250 Melbourne (July 15–19), Macon PPA Challenger (July 17–19), PPA Italy 125 Portoroz (July 22–26), and Leapmotor PPA Asia 500 Singapore Open (July 23–26). Fresh PPA Asia rankings after the Tokyo Open show Tama Shimabukuro rising to world No. 14 in mixed doubles and Mitchell Hargreaves climbing 15 places to No. 24 in men's singles.

newsItems.title: Sun Yingsha Wins Sixth Grand Smash as Brazil Star Contender Nears
newsItems.excerpt: Sun Yingsha edged compatriot Kuai Man 4-3 at WTT United States Smash in Ontario, California, claiming her sixth career Grand Smash title. Japan's Sora Matsushima won men's singles after Wang Chuqin and Lin Shidong both fell in the round of 16. The circuit now shifts to WTT Star Contender Brazil, July 21–26 in São José dos Campos — the first Star Contender in São Paulo state — with Hugo Calderano and Bruna Takahashi headlining.
